name: Metal Support
description: The Metal backend's Linux-safe parts (Sources/CoreRender/Metal): binary16 half-float conversion for filling rgba16Float textures from Float32 buffers and reading them back; MetalCapabilities, the proven op set and health state that RenderDispatcher reads, with the families still compiling in the background held out of its effective supports and the CPU-first families in RenderOp.notOnMetalYet never enabled; SurfaceTiling, the 256 px tile grid a surface's textures follow, on CoreRaster's shared tile math, with the tiles a rect touches, the default memory budget (half the working set, at least one tile) and wholeImageFits, the overflow-checked whole-image buffer-limit check that blur, unsharp and retouch call (w x h x 16 bytes against the device's maxBufferLength); PipelineKey, the identity of one cached compute pipeline (op family plus a short identifier variant) and the kernel function name it maps to; DisplayTable, CoreColor's DisplayTransfer byte rules as Float thresholds (the curve's and the alpha's, plus CoreColor's own linear sRGB to Display P3 matrix, DisplayTransfer.p3FromLinearSRGB, as Float) that the Metal display kernel uploads, with encode, the kernel's per-pixel rule in Swift, outputFits, display's check against the device's buffer limit, and the CPU backend's error for a non-display space; and TileMap, the pixel map of a crop or quarter turn between two tilings (crop rectangles checked with CoreRaster's messages) split into tile-to-tile copy pieces, refusing a tiling of another size than the source it was made for; and CompositeMap, the overlap of a source placed on a backdrop at an integer offset (CoreRaster's in-place composite clip, safe for any Int offset) split into tile-to-tile pieces, with CoreRaster's opacity check; and ResampleTable, one resample axis's taps (CoreRaster's public ResampleFilter.taps, clamp-to-edge indices and weights normalised in Double, flattened and stored as Float, the identity for an unchanged length) as flat arrays the Metal resample kernel uploads, with apply, the kernel's sum in Swift, and peakPixels, the largest buffer a resample allocates, checked against the device limit; and AdjustTable, every tone adjustment as CoreRaster's own adjustment on a probe line run through the CPU backend (per-channel gains for exposure and white balance, a square-root-spaced table over 0...1 with octave tables of the CPU's values outside it, 2^-24 to 2^40 on each side, read by exponent bits and interpolated on the mantissa, an overflowing octave holding the largest finite Float, for levels, curves and contrast, or a gain per Rec. 709 luminance, constant outside 0...1, for highlights/shadows) that the Metal adjust kernel uploads, with apply and map, the kernel's rule in Swift, and unsupported(.color) for every W1 colour case; and OpaqueRows, CoreRaster's opaque-row copy rule (.normal at opacity exactly 1, every stored alpha of the row exactly 1) as per-row flags of a composite piece split into maximal blit and kernel row runs; and BlurTable, CoreRaster's Gaussian blur kernel mirrored exactly (2 ceil(3 sigma) + 1 weights normalised in Double, stored as Float, sigma 0 the single weight 1, CoreRaster's sigma checks and messages, every weight pinned by test to CoreRaster's blur of an impulse) that the Metal blur kernel uploads, with apply, the kernel's clamp-to-edge sum in Swift; and UnsharpRule, the amount and threshold the Metal unsharp kernel uploads (as two Floats), with CoreRaster's amount, threshold and overflow checks and messages, and apply, the kernel's own Float32 rule per premultiplied component (a difference from the blur strictly over Float(threshold) moves it by amount times the difference, one fused multiply-add), which agrees with CoreRaster's Double rule to Float rounding, a difference that close to the threshold taking either branch. Pure Swift integer and floating-point math, no Metal import, so it builds, tests and mutates on Linux.
